scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Petrunino horo originates from the Shopluk region located in middle-west Bulgaria.
Over time, the traditional regional tunes accompanying the dance were documented and compiled widely in Bulgarian dance music collections.
The dance transitioned from rural community settings into the stage repertoire of professional Bulgarian folk troupes, where it remains a central showcase of regional Bulgarian rhythm.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music of Petrunino horo is set in a 12/16 time signature, making it one of two key examples of Bulgarian dances in this meter.
It shares similarities with the Eleno Mome tune, but differentiates itself by splitting the second slow beat into two quick counts, forming the pattern slow, quick, quick, quick, medium.
The pulse is 12/16 at about 130 beats a minute.

The music is defined by a distinctive 12/16 asymmetrical pulse where each measure carries a five-beat breakdown consisting of a long initial beat, three rapid light beats, and a medium concluding beat.
